title: Natural Language Input, Semantic Track Representation, and LLM Inference: Making the Maritime Information Exchange Model Tractable
abstract: arXiv:2608.24892v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We describe a practical architecture for making the Maritime Information Exchange Model (MIEM) and the broader Rich Semantic Track model tractable using current large language model (LLM) technology. The barrier to adoption of semantic track models in defense and law enforcement has been the requirement that operators learn formal ontology languages and manually encode observations as typed logical assertions. We propose eliminating this barrier entirely: operators contribute observations in natural language; an LLM translates these into typed Semantic Assertion Records (SARs), which are named case frames that capture n-ary relations in a single compact structure; a knowledge graph accumulates the SARs; and a second LLM pass performs inference, anomaly detection, and hypothesis ranking over the graph. translated_title: 自然语言输入、语义轨迹表示与LLM推理：使海事信息交换模型变得可行
translated_abstract: 我们描述了一种实用架构，利用当前大语言模型技术，使海事信息交换模型（MIEM）及更广泛的富语义轨迹模型变得可行。在国防和执法领域，采用语义轨迹模型的障碍在于操作员需要学习正式的本体语言，并手动将观察结果编码为类型化逻辑断言。我们提出完全消除这一障碍：操作员以自然语言贡献观察结果；大语言模型将其翻译为类型化语义断言记录（SARs），这些是命名案例框架，以单一紧凑结构捕获n元关系；知识图谱累积SARs；第二次大语言模型通过执行推理、异常检测和假设排名。我们通过两个详细示例（一个9/11时代攻击前指标场景和一个海事货物检查场景）展示了完整流程。
tldr: 该论文提出一种利用大语言模型将自然语言观察自动转换为语义断言记录并执行推理的架构，消除了操作员学习形式化本体语言的障碍，使海事信息交换模型在国防和执法应用中变得实用。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an architecture that uses large language models to automatically convert natural language observations into semantic assertion records and perform inference, eliminating the need for operators to learn formal ontology languages, making the Maritime Information Exchange Model practical for defense and law enforcement applications.
